title: Division on both sides in an automorphism skew-polynomial ring
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $\sigma:k\to k$ a ring automorphism (a bijection preserving addition, multiplication and $1$). Let $A$ be the ring of finite sums $\sum_{i\geq0}a_iF^i$, with coefficientwise addition and multiplication $(aF^i)(bF^j)=a\sigma^i(b)F^{i+j}$. For $h\ne0$ let $\deg h$ be the largest index of a nonzero coefficient. For every $f,g\in A$ with $g\ne0$, there exist $q_L,r_L,q_R,r_R\in A$ such that $$f=q_Lg+r_L=gq_R+r_R,$$ where $r_L=0$ or $\deg r_L<\deg g$, and $r_R=0$ or $\deg r_R<\deg g$.

source.place: Printed p.296, the right division algorithm before Proposition 14.50 and the left division algorithm after it; the same coefficient-cancellation argument for a general coefficient automorphism.

proof.text:
Fix $g
e0$ and put $m=\deg g$, $b=g_m
e0$. We prove both division assertions simultaneously by strong induction on $n=\deg f$ for nonzero $f$, handling $f=0$ separately. If $f=0$, take both quotients and remainders zero. If $f
e0$ and $n<m$, take $q_L=q_R=0$ and $r_L=r_R=f$. In the remaining case $n\ge m$, assume both assertions for every nonzero polynomial of degree less than $n$. Write $a=f_n
e0$ and $d=n-m$.

source.place: Printed p.296, division algorithms immediately before and after Proposition 14.50; expanded coefficient-cancellation induction for a general automorphism.

proof.text: For a left multiple of $g$, set $c=a(\sigma^d(b))^{-1}$ and $t=cF^d$. The inverse exists by [def-weil-field]: $\sigma^d$ is injective and fixes zero, so $\sigma^d(b)\ne0$. Distributivity and the specified monomial multiplication give $tg=\sum_{j=0}^m c\sigma^d(g_j)F^{d+j}$. Thus all coefficients above $n=d+m$ vanish and the coefficient at $n$ is $c\sigma^d(b)=a$. Consequently $h=f-tg$ has all coefficients at indices $\ge n$ zero; hence $h=0$ or $\deg h<n$. In the zero case put $q_L=t$, $r_L=0$. Otherwise the induction hypothesis gives $h=ug+r$, where $r=0$ or $\deg r<m$. Then $f=(t+u)g+r$, so put $q_L=t+u$, $r_L=r$.

source.place: Printed p.296, division algorithms immediately before and after Proposition 14.50; expanded coefficient-cancellation induction for a general automorphism.

proof.text: For a right multiple of $g$, set $c=\sigma^{-m}(b^{-1}a)$ and $t=cF^d$, where $\sigma^{-m}$ denotes the $m$-fold iterate of the inverse automorphism. Here $b^{-1}$ exists by [def-weil-field] and $\sigma^m(c)=b^{-1}a$. The multiplication rule gives $gt=\sum_{j=0}^m g_j\sigma^j(c)F^{j+d}$. All coefficients above $n=m+d$ vanish and the coefficient at $n$ is $b\sigma^m(c)=bb^{-1}a=a$. Thus $h=f-gt$ is zero or has degree less than $n$. If $h=0$, put $q_R=t$, $r_R=0$. Otherwise the induction hypothesis gives $h=gu+r$, with $r=0$ or $\deg r<m$; hence $f=g(t+u)+r$. Put $q_R=t+u$, $r_R=r$.

source.place: Printed p.296, division algorithms immediately before and after Proposition 14.50; expanded coefficient-cancellation induction for a general automorphism.

proof.text: Both recursive calls have strictly smaller nonnegative degree. When $n=0$ and $n\ge m$, necessarily $m=0$ and both differences $h$ are zero, since all their coefficients at indices $\ge0$ vanish. This also supplies the base when the divisor is constant. Strong induction therefore proves both assertions for every nonzero $f$, and step 1 covers zero. The choices on the two sides are independent and together give the required four elements.
